nodeData.note: Many small businesses keep only a cash book, receipts and M-Pesa statements, not full double entry. This topic shows how to rebuild the missing figures and still produce a profit figure and final accounts.

children.note: Records are incomplete when the owner has not kept a full set of double-entry books. The accountant has to fill the gaps from whatever evidence exists.
A business has incomplete records when some books or figures are missing, so a trial balance cannot be drawn up straight from the ledger.

manas.q: What are incomplete records?

children.note: Single entry means each transaction is written down once, usually in a cash book, with no matching second entry. It is simple but does not prove itself the way double entry does.

manas.q: What is single-entry bookkeeping?

children.topic: Typical duka: cash book and M-Pesa
children.note: A duka owner may have a notebook of cash takings, M-Pesa and bank statements, supplier invoices and a stock count. That is often all the accountant gets.
Common reasons: no time or skill for bookkeeping, records lost in fire, flood or theft, or a cashier who stole and destroyed papers.
The owner still needs a profit figure for KRA tax returns, a bank or SACCO loan, and to know if the business is doing well. KASNEB exams test this every few sittings.
Method 1: compare net assets at the start and end of the year (statement of affairs). Method 2: rebuild the accounts to find sales and purchases, then prepare a full income statement.

manas.q: What are the two main approaches to incomplete records?

children.note: A statement of affairs is a list of what the business owns and owes on one date. Comparing two of them shows how much the owner’s stake grew.
A list of assets and liabilities on a given date, made from counts, statements and estimates instead of a ledger. Assets minus liabilities gives the owner’s capital.

manas.q: What is a statement of affairs?

children.note: From topic 2, the accounting equation: assets minus liabilities equals capital. So if we can count net assets, we know the capital.

manas.q: Why do net assets equal capital?

children.note: Opening capital is the net assets at the start of the year: total opening assets less opening liabilities. Exams often hide it and expect you to work it out.

manas.q: How do you find opening capital when it is not given?

children.note: Profit = closing net assets − opening net assets + drawings − capital introduced. A negative answer is a loss.

manas.q: What is the formula for profit from change in net assets?

children.note: Money the owner took out reduced net assets but was not a business loss. Adding it back shows what the business really earned.

manas.q: Why are drawings added back when finding profit from net assets?

children.note: New money the owner put in raised net assets without being earned by trading. Taking it off removes that boost.

manas.q: Why is capital introduced deducted when finding profit from net assets?

children.note: It gives only one profit figure, not sales, cost of sales or expenses. It also cannot show errors or theft, so a full reconstruction is better when evidence allows.
When you have more evidence, rebuild T-accounts and let the missing figure be the balancing number. This is the heart of the topic.
Put every known figure into a T-account. The one missing amount is whatever makes both sides equal.

manas.q: What is the balancing-figure (missing figure) technique?

children.note: Rebuild cash and bank/M-Pesa from opening balance, receipts, payments and closing balance. The balancing figure is often drawings, cash sales or stolen cash.

manas.q: Which figures are usually found as the balancing figure in the cash account?

children.note: Credit sales = closing receivables + cash received from customers + discounts allowed + bad debts written off − opening receivables. This is the receivables control account from topic 12.

manas.q: How do you find credit sales from a receivables account?

children.note: Credit purchases = closing payables + cash paid to suppliers + discounts received − opening payables.

manas.q: How do you find credit purchases from a payables account?

children.note: Add cash sales (from the cash book or M-Pesa till) to credit sales from the receivables account to get total sales.
Expense for the year = cash paid − opening accrual + closing accrual. Topic 7 rules still apply.

manas.q: How do you find an expense when there are opening and closing accruals?

children.note: Expense for the year = cash paid + opening prepayment − closing prepayment.
Use last year’s carrying amount, add assets bought (from the cash book), take off disposals and depreciation (topic 8).
Some owners pay suppliers or themselves from the till before banking. Add those payments back to banked takings to find the true takings.
Gross profit can be expressed against cost (mark-up) or against selling price (margin). Exams use them to find a missing sales or cost of sales figure.
Mark-up is gross profit as a percentage of cost of sales. A 25% mark-up on a KES 800 item adds KES 200, so it sells for KES 1,000.

manas.q: What is mark-up?

children.note: Margin is gross profit as a percentage of sales. The same KES 200 profit on a KES 1,000 sale is a 20% margin.

manas.q: What is gross margin?

children.note: Mark-up 25%: cost 100, profit 25, sales 125. Margin 20%: sales 100, profit 20, cost 80. Write the table first, then scale it.

manas.q: How do you set up a cost structure for mark-up and margin?

children.note: Margin = mark-up ÷ (1 + mark-up). 25% mark-up = 0.25 ÷ 1.25 = 20% margin.

manas.q: How do you convert a mark-up into a margin?

children.note: Mark-up = margin ÷ (1 − margin). 20% margin = 0.20 ÷ 0.80 = 25% mark-up.

manas.q: How do you convert a margin into a mark-up?

children.note: Sales = cost of sales × (1 + mark-up). Cost of sales KES 240,000 at 25% mark-up gives sales of KES 300,000.

children.topic: Finding cost of sales from sales
children.note: Cost of sales = sales × (1 − margin). Sales KES 300,000 at 20% margin gives cost of sales of KES 240,000.

children.topic: Inventory lost by fire or theft
children.note: If stock is burnt or stolen, the count is gone. You estimate what should have been there using the usual margin.
Expected inventory = opening inventory + purchases − cost of sales, where cost of sales comes from sales and the normal margin or mark-up.

manas.q: How do you estimate inventory lost in a fire or theft?

children.note: Take off any stock that was saved or recovered. What is left is the loss to claim from the insurer or write off.
Dr Insurance claim receivable (amount agreed); Dr Income statement for any uninsured part; Cr Purchases (or cost of sales) with the full loss.

manas.q: What entries record inventory lost when part is covered by insurance?

children.note: An uninsured theft is an expense in the income statement. If the owner took the goods, it is drawings instead: Dr Drawings / Cr Purchases.
IAS 2 Inventories says inventory is measured at the lower of cost and net realisable value. The fire estimate is based on cost, matching topic 13.
One year, 1 Jan to 31 Dec, using a cash book, M-Pesa statements and stock counts. All figures in KES and checked to agree.
Fittings 40,000 + inventory 60,000 + receivables 15,000 + cash/M-Pesa 25,000 = 140,000, less payables 20,000. Opening capital = 120,000.
Fittings 36,000 + inventory 75,000 + receivables 18,000 + cash/M-Pesa 41,000 = 170,000, less payables 22,000. Closing net assets = 148,000.
She took 60,000 drawings and put in 20,000 of savings. Profit = 148,000 − 120,000 + 60,000 − 20,000 = 68,000.
Received from customers 210,000, discounts allowed 2,000, bad debt 1,000. Credit sales = 18,000 + 210,000 + 2,000 + 1,000 − 15,000 = 216,000. Add cash sales 84,000: total sales 300,000.
Paid suppliers 190,000 and got 3,000 discounts. Purchases = 22,000 + 190,000 + 3,000 − 20,000 = 195,000.
In: opening 25,000 + cash sales 84,000 + customers 210,000 + capital 20,000 = 339,000. Out: suppliers 190,000 + expenses 48,000 + closing 41,000 = 279,000. Drawings = 60,000.
120,000 − expenses 48,000 − depreciation 4,000 − bad debt 1,000 − discounts allowed 2,000 + discounts received 3,000 = 68,000. Same as the net assets method.

Cost of sales is 240,000 and the owner adds 25% to cost. Sales = 240,000 × 1.25 = 300,000; gross profit 60,000, which is a 20% margin.
Opening stock 50,000, purchases 200,000, sales 240,000 at 20% margin. Cost of sales 192,000, so expected stock 58,000. Stock saved 8,000: loss 50,000.
Insurer agrees to pay 40,000 of the 50,000. Dr Insurance claim 40,000; Dr Income statement (loss) 10,000; Cr Purchases 50,000.

Paid 66,000 rent; 6,000 prepaid at the start, 12,000 prepaid at the end. Expense = 66,000 + 6,000 − 12,000 = 60,000.

Mark-up is on cost, margin is on sales. Using 25% of sales when the question says 25% mark-up gives the wrong cost of sales.

manas.q: What is the most common trap with mark-up and margin?

children.note: Goods the owner took for home use are drawings too. Add them to drawings and remove them from purchases.
Discounts and bad debts reduce receivables without cash. Leave them out and credit sales come out too low.

Payments made straight from takings never reach the bank statement. Add them back or sales will be understated.

children.topic: What iTax is and why it matters
children.note: iTax is KRA's online system for registering, filing returns and paying tax. Almost every working adult in Kenya with a KRA PIN uses it at least once a year.
A KRA PIN is your personal tax number from the Kenya Revenue Authority. You need it for a job, a bank account, a business licence and to file returns.

manas.q: What is a KRA PIN?

children.note: You apply for a PIN online on iTax using your ID details. Once you have it, you keep the same PIN for life.
iTax is KRA's website for tax work: you log in with your PIN and password, file returns, generate payment slips and download certificates.

manas.q: What is iTax?

children.note: Filing on time keeps you free of penalties. A compliant tax record also helps when you need a tender, a loan or a Tax Compliance Certificate.
Filing a return means telling KRA your income and tax. Paying is a separate step. You can file on time and still owe a late payment penalty if you do not pay.

manas.q: Is filing a return the same as paying tax?

children.note: The basic rule is simple: if you have a KRA PIN, you file every year, even when you earned nothing.
Every individual with a KRA PIN must file an individual income tax return every year, even with no income (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Who must file an individual income tax return in Kenya?

children.note: Returns for a year of income can be filed from 1 January to 30 June of the next year (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: When can you file your individual return for a year of income?

children.note: The deadline for the individual return is 30 June of the year after the year of income (check the current KRA rate). For 2025 income, that is 30 June 2026.

manas.q: What is the deadline for individual income tax returns?

children.note: The year of income for individuals is the calendar year, January to December. You file for last year's income in the first half of this year.
People who are exempt from tax must still file a return and enter their Exemption Certificate Number (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Do exempt persons need to file a return?

children.note: For persons with disability, the first KES 150,000 of monthly income is exempt (check the current KRA rate). They file using their Exemption Certificate Number.
Non-residents do not get personal relief (check the current KRA rate). Their tax works differently, so check with KRA or a tax adviser.
There are three common cases: employment income only, employment plus other income, and no income at all (NIL).
Most employees have only a salary. Your employer has already deducted PAYE every month, so the return mostly confirms those figures.
The P9 is your employer's tax deduction card for the year. It shows your pay and the tax deducted. Ask HR or payroll for it early.

manas.q: What is a P9 form?

children.note: Log in to iTax, choose the income tax return for residents, and enter or confirm your pay and tax from the P9. Then submit and save the receipt.
iTax may show your employer's figures already filled in. Check them against your P9 and payslips before you submit.
If you changed jobs, you need a P9 from each employer. Personal relief is claimed once, so you may end up owing a little tax.
If you also earn rent, business profit or side-hustle income, you must add it to the return and work out any extra tax.
Examples: profit from a duka, a matatu, consulting fees, or farm income. Each source is declared on the return.
Work out profit from your sales and expenses records. Guessing leads to errors that KRA can query later.
When other income is added, the total tax is often more than PAYE already paid. The difference is tax due, paid by the deadline.
A NIL return says you had no taxable income for the year. It is the quickest return to file.
File a NIL return if you have a PIN but earned no income in the year (check the current KRA rate). Students and the unemployed often need this.

manas.q: When do you file a NIL return?

children.note: NIL returns can be filed on iTax or on the KRA M-Service App (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Where can you file a NIL return?

children.note: If you had a salary, even for part of the year, a NIL return is wrong. File an employment return with your P9 instead.
An exempt person files the normal return and enters the Exemption Certificate Number given by KRA.
iTax gives an acknowledgement receipt. Save it as proof of filing. If tax is due, the next step is generating a payment slip.

children.topic: Reliefs and how tax is worked out
children.note: Your tax is worked out using tax bands, then reliefs are taken off. Knowing this helps you check your P9.
Annual bands: first 288,000 at 10%; next 100,000 at 25%; next 5,612,000 at 30%; next 3,600,000 at 32.5%; above 9,600,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the annual individual tax bands?

children.note: Monthly bands: first 24,000 at 10%; next 8,333 at 25%; next 467,667 at 30%; next 300,000 at 32.5%; above 800,000 at 35% (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What are the monthly individual tax bands?

children.note: Personal relief is KES 28,800 a year, or 2,400 a month (check the current KRA rate). It is taken off the tax for resident individuals.

manas.q: How much is personal relief?

children.note: Insurance relief is 15% of premiums on life, education (10+ years) or health policies, up to KES 60,000 a year (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How is insurance relief worked out?

children.note: Tax payable = tax from the bands minus reliefs. Then subtract PAYE already deducted to see if you owe more or nothing.

manas.q: How do you get tax payable from tax on bands?

children.note: After filing, any tax due is paid using a payment slip from iTax.
On iTax, choose to make a payment, pick the tax and period, and generate the slip (check the current KRA rate). The slip shows the amount and a Payment Registration Number.

manas.q: What do you need from iTax before paying tax?

children.note: The PRN is the reference number on your payment slip. It links your money to your tax so KRA can credit your account.

manas.q: What is a PRN?

children.note: Use M-Pesa Paybill 222222 (the unified Government paybill). The account number is the PRN on the slip (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: How do you pay KRA tax by M-Pesa?

children.note: Take the slip to an appointed KRA bank and pay over the counter (check the current KRA rate). Keep the bank receipt.
Save the M-Pesa message or bank receipt with the slip. They are your proof if iTax does not show the payment.
Late filing and late payment are charged separately. You can be charged both.
For individuals: the higher of 5% of the tax due or KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate). Even a NIL filer can be charged the KES 2,000.

manas.q: What is the late filing penalty for individuals?

children.note: If tax is paid after the due date: a penalty of 5% of the tax due (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What is the late payment penalty?

children.note: Interest of 1% per month is charged on unpaid tax until it is paid (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: What interest does KRA charge on unpaid tax?

children.note: File by 30 June and pay by the same date. If you cannot pay in full, file anyway, so you avoid the late filing penalty.
Real numbers, step by step. Rates as confirmed on kra.go.ke today; always check the current KRA rate.
Mary earns KES 600,000 a year in salary. Let us work out her tax for the year.
117,400 − personal relief 28,800 = KES 88,600 tax for the year (check the current KRA rate).
If her P9 shows PAYE of 88,600, she owes nothing more. This is a simplified example that ignores other deductions.
Late filing penalty is the higher of 5% of tax due or KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate).
5% × 30,000 = 1,500. KES 2,000 is higher, so the penalty is KES 2,000.
5% × 100,000 = 5,000. That is higher than 2,000, so the penalty is KES 5,000.
Tax due is zero, so 5% is zero. The penalty is the minimum KES 2,000.
Otieno owes KES 60,000 on his duka profit. He files and pays 3 months after the deadline.
Higher of 5% × 60,000 = 3,000 or 2,000. Penalty = KES 3,000 (check the current KRA rate).
5% × 60,000 = KES 3,000 (check the current KRA rate).
1% × 60,000 × 3 months = KES 1,800 (check the current KRA rate).
60,000 + 3,000 + 3,000 + 1,800 = KES 67,800. Filing and paying on time would have saved KES 7,800.
Jane pays health and life premiums. See how the KES 60,000 cap works (check the current KRA rate).
15% × 48,000 = 7,200. Below 60,000, so her relief is KES 7,200 for the year.
15% × 500,000 = 75,000. That is above the cap, so relief is limited to KES 60,000.
Good records make filing quick and protect you if KRA asks questions.
P9 forms, payslips, filing receipts, payment slips, M-Pesa or bank receipts, insurance premium certificates and business sales and expense records.
For a duka or matatu, keep daily sales, receipts for expenses and bank or M-Pesa statements. These support the profit you declare.
Make one folder, paper or on your phone, for each year of income. File everything as it comes in.
Keep your PIN and password safe and private. Never share your password, even with a cyber café attendant.

People with no income think they need not file. They do, and a late NIL return can still cost KES 2,000 (check the current KRA rate).

manas.q: Can you be penalised for a late NIL return?

children.note: Forgetting insurance relief on a qualifying policy means paying more tax than you should. Keep the premium certificate.
Typing pay or PAYE that differs from the P9 can show tax due that is not real, or trigger a query. Copy figures carefully.
If you were employed, a NIL return is wrong. You must declare your employment income.
iTax gets busy near the deadline. File early in the window so problems can be fixed in time.
Submitting the return does not pay the tax. Generate the slip and pay, or penalty and interest will build up.
